objectives: Explain the per-token MLP and its expand/contract shape
State why the FFN holds most parameters

slides.title: Part 1 — Where the parameters actually live
slides.body: Attention gets the headlines, but the feed-forward network (FFN) holds most of a transformer layer's parameters and most of its FLOPs. A useful mantra: **attention mixes tokens; the FFN mixes features.**

slides.title: The parameter budget
slides.body:
For $d_{model}=4096$ with the standard 4× expansion:

- $W_1$: $[4096, 16384]$ ≈ 67M params
- $W_2$: $[16384, 4096]$ ≈ 67M params

vs attention's four $[4096,4096]$ projections ≈ 67M total. So the **FFN is ~2/3 of the per-layer parameters**, and where most learned *knowledge* (facts, patterns) is stored. Attention decides *what to look at*; the FFN decides *what to compute* with it.

slides.title: What the FFN computes
slides.body:
A 2-layer MLP applied **independently to every token position**:

$$\text{FFN}(x)=W_2\,\phi(W_1 x + b_1) + b_2$$

1. **Up-project** $x$ to a wider hidden dim (≈ 4×).
2. Apply a **nonlinearity** $\phi$ (ReLU → GELU → SwiGLU).
3. **Down-project** back to $d_{model}$.

Crucially: **no cross-token interaction.** Position 5 is processed without ever seeing position 4 or 6. All token mixing happens in attention; the FFN is the per-token transform that gives the network its nonlinear expressive power.

question.question: Inside the FFN, can token i's output depend on token j's input?
options: No — the FFN is applied independently per token; cross-token mixing happens only in attention
Yes — that's the point of the transformer
Yes, but only within an attention window
question.explanation: The FFN shares one MLP across positions but runs it on each token independently. Remove attention and keep only FFNs and the model loses all ability to use context — every token would map through the MLP in isolation.

slides.title: ReLU → GELU → SwiGLU
slides.body:
Explore the activation gallery on the right.

- **ReLU** $\max(0,x)$ — simple, fast, but dead neurons (zero gradient for negative input).
- **GELU** $x\,\Phi(x)$ — smooth, slightly negative for slightly-negative $x$; better gradient flow; beat ReLU for LMs (BERT, GPT-2).
- **SwiGLU** — a *gated* unit: split the up-projection, gate one half by Swish, multiply by the other: $(\text{Swish}(xW)\odot xV)W_2$. The gate lets the FFN selectively activate features; consistently best at fixed compute (LLaMA, modern Mistral). LLaMA uses ~2.7× expansion *because* the gate adds an extra projection.

question.question: Ablate ALL FFN layers, keep only attention. What happens?
options: Token mixing still works, but per-token transforms collapse toward linear combinations of values — capacity drops sharply
question.explanation: Attention is essentially a (softmax-weighted) linear average of values. Without the FFN's nonlinearity the per-token function is mostly linear, so the model loses most of its ability to compute non-trivial features even though tokens can still exchange information.

question.question: Why is the FFN hidden dimension typically ~4× d_model?
options: Empirically the sweet spot — enough room for rich nonlinear features without spending parameters that don't help
It must equal the number of attention heads
It is required for residual connections to work
question.explanation: The up-projection lifts each token into a higher-dim space where useful features become separable; the activation selects them; the down-projection collapses back. ~4× is the empirical balance — smaller underfits the needed nonlinearity, larger wastes parameters. (MoE breaks this: huge per-expert FFNs, but only a few experts active per token.)

question.question: Derive the position-wise FFN
question.goal: From: give each token its own nonlinear feature mixer between attention layers.

steps.prompt: Why expand to a wider hidden layer then project back (d → 4d → d)?
steps.motivation: A wider hidden layer + nonlinearity adds per-token capacity to recombine features; projecting back keeps the residual stream width.

options: Width + nonlinearity adds representational capacity per token
It is required for residual connections

steps.reveal: Expand→nonlinearity→contract is a per-token MLP that adds capacity while preserving width.

steps.prompt: Write FFN(x) with one hidden ReLU layer.
steps.motivation: Two linear maps with a nonlinearity between them is the minimal universal per-token transform.
steps.reveal: FFN(x)=W₂·ReLU(W₁x+b₁)+b₂, applied identically at every position.

question.question: Push the hidden multiplier up and watch the FFN parameter count (millions) — it dominates the block.
question.explanation: At d=512, m=4 the FFN alone is ~2M params per block — most transformer parameters live here, not in attention.

question.prompt: Explain the FFN to your pet: what shape it is, why the widening, and why it is per-token.

rubricCriteria.description: a small MLP applied independently to every token (position-wise)
holds the majority of the block's parameters

question.question: Diagnose what breaks.
question.scenario: Profiling shows the FFN is ~2/3 of per-block FLOPs and params. A teammate proposes deleting it for speed.

rubricCriteria.description: attention's value aggregation is a (softmax-weighted) average — largely linear, cross-token
the FFN supplies the per-token NONLINEAR transformation/capacity
removing it collapses representational power; quality craters despite the speedup

question.explanation: Speed isn't free here: the FFN is where per-token nonlinear capacity lives. Attention mostly mixes; the FFN mostly transforms.

hints: Is a weighted average of values linear or nonlinear?
Where does per-token nonlinearity enter the block?
slides.workedSolution: Attention aggregates values nearly linearly across tokens. The FFN is the block's per-token nonlinear transform; without it the model loses most capacity.

question.question: Attention mixes info across tokens. What unique role does the FFN add?
question.explanation: Attention is a softmax-weighted average of values — largely linear mixing across positions. The FFN (expand→ReLU→contract) is the per-token nonlinearity.

slides.title: What to carry forward
slides.body:
- FFN = up-project → nonlinearity → down-project, **per token** (no cross-token mixing).
- It holds **~2/3** of a layer's parameters and most stored knowledge.
- **~4× expansion** is the empirical sweet spot; **SwiGLU** is the modern default activation.
- Remove it and the model loses its per-token nonlinear power.

**Next:** [Residual connections](/wiki/residual-connections) and [layer normalization](/wiki/layer-normalization) — the glue that makes stacking these blocks trainable — then the full [transformer block](/wiki/transformer-block).
